front: What is the difference between the abscissa and the ordinate of a point (x, y)?
back:
• Abscissa (x): Perpendicular distance of the point from the y-axis (measured along the x-axis).
• Ordinate (y): Perpendicular distance of the point from the x-axis (measured along the y-axis).
note: Exam tip: Remember alphabetical order: (Abscissa, Ordinate) corresponds to (x, y).

front: What are the coordinates of the Origin, and what are the general forms of points on the x-axis and y-axis?
back:
• Origin: O(0, 0).
• Point on x-axis: (x, 0) (ordinate is always 0).
• Point on y-axis: (0, y) (abscissa is always 0).
note: Points lying directly on the coordinate axes do NOT belong to any quadrant!

front: State the sign signs (x, y) for points in Quadrants I, II, III, and IV.
back:
• Quadrant I: (+, +)
• Quadrant II: (-, +)
• Quadrant III: (-, -)
• Quadrant IV: (+, -)
note: Numbered counter-clockwise starting from the top-right quadrant.

front:
What is the perpendicular distance of the point P(-5, 7) from:
(i) the x-axis, and (ii) the y-axis?
back:
• Distance from x-axis = |y| = |7| = 7 units.
• Distance from y-axis = |x| = |-5| = 5 units.
note: Distance is always a non-negative scalar quantity!

front: Can the points (3, -4) and (-4, 3) represent the same point on a Cartesian plane?
back: No! An ordered pair depends strictly on order. (3, -4) lies in Quadrant IV, whereas (-4, 3) lies in Quadrant II.
note: (a, b) = (b, a) if and only if a = b.
